title: Telemetry fidelity exercise and dashboard verification playbook
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Summary

This playbook documents a repeatable, operator-driven exercise to validate telemetry signal fidelity end-to-end, confirm dashboard correctness, and verify alert routing and severity mapping under controlled synthetic load and degradation. The audience is platform operators, observability engineers, and service owners.

Objectives

- Prove metric fidelity from exporters through ingestion, aggregation, and long-term storage.
- Ensure dashboards render correct dimensions (tenant, region, model_variant) and align with raw metric timelines.
- Validate alert firing behavior, routing, and notification payloads for latency, error-rate, and cost anomalies.
- Produce concrete remediation items with owners and validation criteria tied back to the Platform roadmap.

Scope

Included components:
- runtime-metrics-exporter (per-host exporter)
- metric-ingest (collector front-end)
- scribe-proxy (auth + buffering)
- sli-aggregator (rollups and SLI computation)
- telemetry-indexer (long-term store and query)
- operator-console (dashboards and alert delivery)

Out of scope:
- External SaaS telemetry providers (we only validate consumer contract adapters)

Prerequisites

- Staging cluster: staging-telemetry-sim (k8s namespace telemetry-sim)
- Access: platform-operators, telemetry-admin groups
- Binaries/CLIs: kubectl, curl, jq, oc (if applicable)
- Synthetic workload image: registry.redwood-internal/telemetry-sim:stable-202410
- Runbook artifacts present in repo: synthetic-workloads.yaml, dashboard-validation-plan.md

Roles and responsibilities

- Runbook owner: Aisha Kumar (Platform Observability)
- Telemetry SME: Jonah Perez (Infra Instrumentation)
- Dashboard SME: Mei Chen (Developer Experience)
- On-call escalation: eng-platform oncall rotation (primary: @oncall-platform)

Pre-exercise checks (T minus 60 -> T minus 15)

1) Verify cluster and control plane health
   - kubectl -n telemetry-sim get pods -l app=metric-ingest
   - curl -fsS https://operator-console.staging/health | jq '.'
2) Capture 15m baseline windows for key metrics
   - curl -sS "https://sli-aggregator.staging/api/v1/query_range?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le,service))&start=$(date -u -d '15 minutes ago' +%s)&end=$(date -u +%s)" > /tmp/baseline_p95.json
3) Export dashboard JSON and current alert ruleset
   - curl -sS https://operator-console.staging/api/dashboards/traffic-overview > /tmp/dashboard_traffic_overview.json
   - curl -sS https://operator-console.staging/api/alerts > /tmp/alerts_ruleset.json

Controlled exercise plan (T0 -> T+60 minutes)

We run a sequence of controlled phases. Each phase includes a synthetic workload pattern, an induced degradation (where applicable), and a 5-minute observation window. Record all observations in the exercise log and attach artifacts.

Phase A: Baseline confirmation (10 minutes)
- Start low-rate steady producers to ensure telemetry flows end-to-end.
- Commands:
  - kubectl apply -n telemetry-sim -f synthetic-workloads-baseline.yaml
  - kubectl exec -n telemetry-sim deployment/telemetry-injector -- /app/bin/generate --rate 50 --tenants tenant-a,tenant-b --duration 15m &
- Expected outcomes:
  - exporter metrics present with correct tenant labels
  - dashboards show baseline equivalent to /tmp/baseline_p95.json

Phase B: Intermittent ingestion pressure (15 minutes)
- Introduce CPU throttling on metric-ingest to 40% of nominal CPU quota using capacity-sim controller.
- Introduce a 1.5x RSA burst producer pattern to spike traffic intermittently.
- Commands:
  - curl -X POST https://capacity-sim.staging/api/v1/sweep -d '{"service":"metric-ingest","cpu_pct":40,"duration_mins":15}'
  - kubectl exec -n telemetry-sim deployment/telemetry-injector -- /app/bin/generate --pattern burst --rate 150 --duration 15m &
- Validation checklist:
  - Confirm metric-ingest CPU chart tracks to ~40% on the operator-console.
  - Verify ingest-latency-warning alert fires if p95 > 120ms and not sooner.
  - Compare raw request_latency_ms_bucket time series to sli-aggregator rollups: acceptable delta <= 8%.

Phase C: Partial store degradation with tag drift (20 minutes)
- Simulate packet loss at scribe-proxy (2% drop) and increase telemetry-indexer write latency by 500ms.
- Commands (simulation):
  - curl -X POST https://scribe-proxy.staging/api/simulate -d '{"drop_pct":2}'
  - curl -X POST https://telemetry-indexer.staging/simulate-latency -d '{"latency_ms":500}'
- Validation checklist:
  - Verify tenant and model_variant tags persist through scribe-proxy; if tags drop, capture first failing pod and logs.
  - Ensure SLI aggregator exposes partial rollups and that dashboards annotate data gaps.

Phase D: Severe backpressure and graceful fallback (15 minutes)
- Increase metric-ingest CPU throttle to 90% and temporarily disable non-critical indexer workers to force partial-rollup fallback.
- Expected outcomes:
  - Alerting: critical path alerts should escalate (pagerduty) for ingest-backfill-required.
  - Operator-console should display degraded mode with clear guidance to trigger operator fallback.

Metric mapping and acceptance matrix

Metric source | metric name | derived SLI | acceptable delta | owner
--------------|-------------|-------------|------------------|------
runtime-metrics-exporter | request_latency_ms_bucket | request_latency_p95 | <= 8% | Jonah Perez
metric-ingest | ingest_queue_length | ingest_latency_alert | queue growth correlated with p95 | Aisha Kumar
sli-aggregator | token_cost_per_request | token_cost_anomaly | <= 5% | finance-product

Alert examples (canonical snippets)

- ingest-latency-warning
  - expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 0.12
  - for: 3m
  - severity: warning
  - notify: pager-duty:platform-operators

- ingest-backfill-required
  - expr: increase(ingest_backpressure_total[10m]) > 0
  - for: 0m
  - severity: critical
  - notify: slack:#platform-ops, email:telemetry-sre@example.com

Artifact capture (minimum required)

- /tmp/baseline_p95.json (baseline time window)
- /tmp/dashboard_traffic_overview.json (dashboard JSON export)
- /tmp/alerts_ruleset.json (alerts at start-of-exercise)
- /tmp/alerts_snapshot.json (active alerts captured during exercise)
- /tmp/rollups_15m.json (sli-aggregator rollups)
- /tmp/metric_ingest_tail.log (last 500 lines)

Commands for quick capture:
- kubectl -n telemetry-sim logs deployment/metric-ingest --tail=500 > /tmp/metric_ingest_tail.log
- curl -sS https://sli-aggregator.staging/api/v1/rollups?window=15m > /tmp/rollups_15m.json
- curl -sS https://operator-console.staging/api/alerts/active > /tmp/alerts_snapshot.json

Operator quick checklist

- [ ] Cluster pre-checks passed and baseline captured
- [ ] Synthetic producers running for each phase
- [ ] Phase A executed and observations recorded
- [ ] Phase B executed and observations recorded
- [ ] Phase C executed and observations recorded
- [ ] Phase D executed and observations recorded
- [ ] Alerts and dashboard mismatch tickets created (if any)
- [ ] Artifacts uploaded to /mnt/platform-sim-artifacts/<run-id>
- [ ] Retrospective scheduled within 48 hours

Retrospective template

1) Executive summary and hypotheses tested
2) Observed mismatches and their severity (e.g., missing tenant label, p95 divergence > 8%)
3) Root cause hypotheses with evidence attachments
4) Action items: owner, priority, due date, validation criteria
5) Risk assessment and customer impact mapping

Sample action item format

- id: TELE-2024-101
- title: Restore tenant label propagation through scribe-proxy
- owner: Mei Chen
- priority: P1
- due: 2024-12-05
- validation: run Phase C simulation and confirm no missing tenant labels and <= 2% tag loss

Roadmap alignment and cadence

- Runbook cadence: quarterly or prior to any major telemetry pipeline change.
- Backlog mapping: obs:telemetry-fidelity (triage board) and platform roadmap Q1/Q2 2025 for SLI hardening and indexer improvements.

Related artifacts and pages

- /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/telemetry-preproc-compatibility-matrix-2024
- /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/operator-telemetry-quality-kpi-library-2025

Appendix: troubleshooting notes and common pitfalls

- If rollups diverge: verify ingestion timestamps and timezone normalization (UTC expected).
- If tenant tags are missing: check scribe-proxy header preservation, network proxies, and envoy filters that may strip headers.
- When alerts fire but dashboards do not reflect expected values: confirm dashboard query time range and panel resolution match the metric scrape intervals.
